explain.say: A bruise forms when a knock breaks tiny blood vessels under the skin without breaking the skin. Blood leaks into the tissue and shows through as a red or bluish patch.

faq.a: A bruise is blood that has leaked from tiny broken blood vessels into the tissue under unbroken skin. The pooled blood shows through the skin as a coloured patch.

faq.q: Why are new bruises purple or blue?
faq.a: Fresh leaked blood is red, but once it loses its oxygen it turns darker. Seen through layers of skin, this dark blood looks purple or bluish.
asks: Why are bruises dark at first?

faq.q: Why do bruises turn green and yellow?
faq.a: White blood cells break down the haemoglobin from the trapped blood. It changes first into green biliverdin and then into yellow bilirubin, so the colours show the clean-up in progress.
asks: Why does a bruise go yellow?

faq.q: How does a bruise go away?
faq.a: White blood cells called macrophages eat the leaked blood and break down its pigments, which are then carried away in the bloodstream and removed by the liver.
asks: How long does a bruise last?

faq.q: Why do some people bruise more easily?
faq.a: Skin thickness, the strength of small blood vessels and age all play a part. Older people bruise more easily because their skin is thinner and has less cushioning fat.
asks: Why do I bruise so easily?

facts: Haemoglobin is broken down into green biliverdin and then yellow bilirubin.
The yellow pigment bilirubin is the same one that gives yellow colour to skin in jaundice.

quiz.say: A bruise turns green after a few days. What is causing the green colour?
quiz.show: The green colour in a healing bruise comes from…

options.show: Biliverdin made as haemoglobin breaks down
options.say: Biliverdin made as haemoglobin breaks down

quiz.why: White blood cells break haemoglobin into green biliverdin, a sign the bruise is being cleared away.

wrong.1: A bruise is under unbroken skin; the colour change is normal clean-up, not germs.
wrong.2: Fresh blood is red or purple, not green.
